    Dune Meadows II: Sequential Multifactor Models

    dune-multifactor.Rmd

    permanova_fixed() implements Type-I, or sequential, sums of squares. In the unbalanced dune data, each term is adjusted for terms that precede it, so term order is part of the hypothesis.

    management_first <- permanova_fixed(
  distance = bray,
  formula = ~ Management + Moisture,
  data = dune.env,
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260718
)
management_first$table
#>         term df       ss        ms pseudo_f p_perm
#> 1 Management  3 1.468592 0.4895306 3.790725  0.005
#> 2   Moisture  3 1.151622 0.3838741 2.972564  0.005
#> 3   Residual 13 1.678808 0.1291391       NA     NA
#> 4      Total 19 4.299022        NA       NA     NA

    Reversing the terms leaves the full-model residual unchanged but reallocates sequential sums of squares.

    moisture_first <- permanova_fixed(
  distance = bray,
  formula = ~ Moisture + Management,
  data = dune.env,
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260718
)
moisture_first$table
#>         term df       ss        ms pseudo_f p_perm
#> 1   Moisture  3 1.728165 0.5760550 4.460734  0.005
#> 2 Management  3 0.892049 0.2973497 2.302554  0.010
#> 3   Residual 13 1.678808 0.1291391       NA     NA
#> 4      Total 19 4.299022        NA       NA     NA
    rbind(
  management_then_moisture = management_first$table$ss[1:2],
  moisture_then_management = moisture_first$table$ss[1:2]
)
#>                              [,1]     [,2]
#> management_then_moisture 1.468592 1.151622
#> moisture_then_management 1.728165 0.892049

    The Design Object exposes rank and estimability before inference.

    dune_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ Management + Moisture,
  data = dune.env,
  distance = bray
)
dune_design
#> Canonical PERMANOVA design
#> Observations: 20  Fixed rank: 7 
#> Fixed: Management, Moisture 
#> Random: (none) 
#> Euclidean distance: FALSE 
#> Warnings: Dissimilarity is non-Euclidean; negative eigenvalues were retained.
dune_design$estimability
#> $fixed_rank
#> [1] 7
#> 
#> $fixed_columns
#> [1] 7
#> 
#> $aliased
#> character(0)
#> 
#> $terms
#> Management   Moisture 
#>       TRUE       TRUE

    For the same term order, the observed sequential pseudo-F values can be checked against vegan::adonis2(by = "terms").

    adonis2(
  bray ~ Management + Moisture,
  data = dune.env,
  permutations = 0,
  by = "terms"
)
#> Permutation test for adonis under reduced model
#> Terms added sequentially (first to last)
#> Permutation: free
#> Number of permutations: 0
#> 
#> adonis2(formula = bray ~ Management + Moisture, data = dune.env, permutations = 0, by = "terms")
#>            Df SumOfSqs      R2      F Pr(>F)
#> Management  3   1.4686 0.34161 3.7907      1
#> Moisture    3   1.1516 0.26788 2.9726      1
#> Residual   13   1.6788 0.39051              
#> Total      19   4.2990 1.00000

    These are unrestricted fixed-effect tests. Adding a grouping variable to the formula would require a hypothesis-specific mixed inference engine, not merely a different permutation argument.
